title: JRE 2330 - Bono
guestBio: Bono is the lead singer of the rock band U2, as well as an activist and author. His memoir, "Bono: Stories of Surrender," is available wherever books are sold. Watch the companion film on Apple TV+, and the soundtrack is available digitally and on limited edition vinyl.

Conversation covers U2's evolution as a band and their impact on rock music over multiple decades

They explore the creative process behind U2's most iconic albums and the stories behind their biggest hits
recap:
Joe sits down with Bono, the legendary frontman of U2, to discuss his new memoir 'Stories of Surrender' which offers an intimate look at his life, career, and personal journey. The conversation ranges across Bono's decades-long career as one of rock music's most influential voices, touching on how U2 evolved from their early days to becoming a global phenomenon.

Bono opens up about the philosophy behind the memoir's title, exploring themes of surrender and vulnerability that have shaped his approach to both music and activism. He shares insights into his creative process and how personal experiences have informed U2's most iconic work. The discussion naturally flows into his activism efforts, with Bono explaining how his platform has allowed him to advocate for causes he's passionate about, including global health and poverty alleviation.

Throughout the episode, Joe and Bono dive into the spiritual and philosophical elements that underscore his work. Bono discusses how faith and introspection have guided major decisions in his life and career. They talk about the pressures of fame, the responsibility that comes with having a global platform, and how he's learned to balance his role as an entertainer with his work as an advocate for change.

The conversation also touches on U2's legacy and influence on rock music, with Bono reflecting on some of the band's most memorable moments and how they've managed to remain relevant across multiple generations. He discusses the challenge of creating meaningful art in an ever-changing industry and what drives him to continue after so many years in the spotlight.

quotes: The memoir is called 'Stories of Surrender' because it's about learning to let go of control and accepting what life brings.
U2 was never just a band, it was always about something bigger than ourselves.
Faith and spirituality aren't separate from my art, they're central to everything I do.
You realize as you get older that your platform is a responsibility, not just a privilege.
The best songs come from a place of honesty and vulnerability, not from trying to be perfect.
